title: Seller lab playbook - ops hands-on (draft)
content:
Objective: quick, hands-on workshop for platform sellers and SEs to run a 90-minute lab that demonstrates how Redwood routing + canary policies + fallback variants keep customer flows online while tuning for cost. This is a field-ready playbook (draft) — minimal slides, heavy on facilitator notes and step-by-step exercises.

Audience: platform sellers, solutions engineers, integration architects, 1 SRE from prospect (optional). Best for accounts evaluating Dedicated or Private with strict SLA/cost requirements.

High-level goals:
- Show measurable impact of routing policies and model variants on latency and unit cost.
- Give an operator-run checklist to execute a canary and safe rollback.
- Arm sellers with demo artifacts and objection responses for latency/cost/regulatory questions.

90-minute agenda (timeboxed)
- 00:00–00:08 — Kickoff (value thread + 3 slide context): why routing matters (latency/cost/reliability). Quick product positioning lines.
- 00:08–00:18 — Live topology walkthrough: hosted vs. dedicated vs. private (diagram + routing lanes). Annotated with common customer constraints.
- 00:18–00:28 — Canary pattern demo (walkthrough): explain policy components (traffic %, health checks, fallback map).
- 00:28–00:50 — Lab 1 (hands-on): run a canary on the console (or scripted simulation). Measure latency  p50/p95, token cost delta.
- 00:50–01:05 — Lab 2 (failure injection): simulate region outage / capacity throttling -> observe auto-fallback. Capture artifacts (logs, traces).
- 01:05–01:18 — Lab 3 (economics tuning): change batching/quantization profile -> observe cost vs. degredation. Quick decision heuristics.
- 01:18–01:28 — Wrap: success criteria, customer next steps, pilot checklist.
- 01:28–01:30 — Q&A and handoff (next actions).

Materials required (pre-work checklist for hosts):
- Redwood demo org with a small sample model that supports two variants (fast/cheap and high-quality).
- Console access: canary controls, routing policy editor, logs & trace viewer.
- Synthetic load generator script (node/python) and sample prompt set (10 prompts).
- Pre-created dashboards: latency heatmap, token-cost per 1k requests, canary health stream.
- Slack or Zoom with screen sharing and a co-host SRE.

Lab exercise details (facilitator notes):
- Lab 1 (Canary run)
  - Step 1: Create canary with 5% traffic to variant-B (cheaper quantized model).
  - Step 2: Observe p50/p95 on dashboard for baseline vs canary for 10 minutes. Take screenshot.
  - Expected: small p50 change, p95 might drift if batch size changes. Capture token cost per minute.
  - Talking points: how to pick percentage & ramp cadence, how to use pre-checks (latency gating).

- Lab 2 (Failure injection)
  - Step 1: On infra sim: throttle capacity in primary region or flip a routing tag to make region unavailable.
  - Step 2: Watch automatic routing fallback to secondary variant/region.
  - Expected: traffic reroutes within policy SLO, minimal user-visible errors. Capture traces showing request path change.
  - Troubles: if fallback triggers errors, show rollback steps (roll canary back, re-route to reserved capacity).

- Lab 3 (Economics tuning)
  - Step 1: Change batching target and enable the quantization profile for the cheaper variant. Run the prompt set.
  - Step 2: Compare quality (sample threshold) and unit-cost.
  - Decision heuristic: If quality degradation < X% and cost savings > Y%, recommend enabling at 100% for non-safety-critical routes.

Facilitator scripts & slide notes (short bullets):
- Slide: "Why routing matters" -> 2 anecdotes: (1) a fin-tech app that needed p95 < 300ms, (2) an ecomm recommender where token cost mattered at scale. Keep <30s each.
- Slide: "Canary controls" -> demo live UI; point out health checks and automatic rollback toggle.
- Slide: "Fallbacks & graceful degradation" -> script: "If the expensive model trips, we route to a smaller model variant AND tag the payload for post-hoc review."
- Objection handling quick lines:
  - "What about compliance?" -> highlight Private deployment + KMS + audit logs.
  - "We can't lose accuracy" -> show canary quality gating and evalsets + rollback.
  - "Cost unpredictability" -> show token-level cost breakdown and reserved capacity pricing.

Artifacts to hand prospect after session (deliverables):
- Pilot checklist (14-day onramp plan).
- Pre-populated canary policy yaml + sample prompt set.
- Dashboard snapshots and a short csv of measured latency/cost deltas.
- Follow-up proposal template (SaaS credits + reserved-capacity estimate).

Success criteria (for workshop to be considered a win):
- Prospect-run canary started during session and observed measurable cost delta (yes/no).
- Prospect SRE comfortable with fallback steps (verbal confirmation).
- Agreed next step: pilot commit or 14-day technical evaluation.

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self):
- Add a short script to automatically capture canary metrics and generate a 1-page summary (TODO: GH PR).
- Confirm access pattern for Private demo (air-gapped customers) — need a sanitized guide.
- Create a one-slide decision lens for CFO finance pitch (cost vs uptime).
- Hook a sample Prometheus exporter -> link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/demo-monitoring (draft).

Appendix: quick checklists for sellers
- Pre-call: confirm the prospect can run a small test container or grant console demo access.
- On-call: if demo fails, pivot to pre-recorded dashboard video. Keep failure script ready.
- Post-call: send tailored pilot checklist + billing estimate within 48 hours.

Speaker notes style: informal, energetic, short cues (e.g., "pause -> ask: what is your p95 pain threshold?").

Retention: keep this deck under 6 slides in live session. Most of the value is in the lab artifacts and the post-session deliverables.

File notes: this is a rough field draft. Use for upcoming west-coast seller bootcamp. Will iterate after 3 runs and convert to a polished slide deck and a one-page seller cheat sheet.
